items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The names say what they do (compile_json_path_final_key, HasKeyOrArrayIndex), the new hook has a short explanatory comment, and the formatting matches the surrounding json.py code.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: It adds an overridable hook and a 3-line subclass, reuses compile_json_path for the leading path segments, and has no per-backend copies of the path logic, dead code or debug leftovers.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: It uses json.dumps(key_transform) to quote the key safely, adds no exception handling or magic constants, and the hidden tests pass (F2P 2/2, P2P 78/78).

items.name: Array-index semantics kept for isnull / exact=None paths
items.name_zh: isnull / exact=None 路径保留数组下标语义
items.evidence: The final has_key key is compiled as ".%s" % json.dumps(...) in the shared HasKeyLookup.as_sql. HasKeyOrArrayIndex is used in KeyTransformIsNull.as_oracle/as_sqlite and KeyTransformExact.as_oracle, so ints there still mean array indices. Intermediate segments are unchanged.
